answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like a garden where every plot costs a deposit and weeds forfeit theirs. A newcomer starts with a tiny trust budget that grows only through verified, useful work, so a flood of fresh accounts is expensive and slow. Unlike a fable where a comet passes once and vanishes, the stake stays bonded and auditable, so an attacker must pay real money per fake identity and lose it when fraud is exposed.
